answer: Sybil resistance rests on age-weighted, non-transferable standing: a new identity starts at zero influence and gains weight only by surviving many epochs of graded, non-duplicated writing, so a thousand clones from one attacker sit at zero tonight. Standing cannot be bought or merged, so the only route is time. Each dawn he must pay for fresh text per identity, and every submission meets a randomly drawn jury that slashes copies to nothing. One honest answer costs an hour; ten thousand clones cost ten thousand hours for copper-level upside, while the pool pays saffron-priced labor only.
